newsitem.title: USA: Aspen to take $750,000 Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: Aspen to take $750,000 Q2 charge.

text.p: Aspen Technology Inc said on Tuesday that it would take a $750,000 one-time charge for the acquisition of the process-control division of Cambridge Control Ltd.
Aspen, which supplies computer-aided chemical engineering, on-line automation and process information management software and services, said in a statement that it paid $1.9 million for the unit.
Aspen will account for the acquisition as a purchase transaction. Excluding the charge, it did not expect the deal to dilute fiscal 1997 earnings.
Aspen said it would take the charge in its second fiscal quarter ending December .3
Cambridge is a consulting and systems integration company based in Britain.
Mary Palermo, Aspen Technology's executive vice president and chief financial officer, said the acquisition would enable the company's European operations to contribute to earnings.
In a separate news release, Aspen said it completed the acquisition of B-JAC International Inc, a Virginia-based supplier of detailed heat exchanger modeling software.
The company said it would acquire all of B-JAC's stock for $3.4 million. It will treat the purchase as a stock-for-stock pooling transaction.
The acquisition was not expected to dilute earnings in fiscal 1997, Palermo said.
